Q2. Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".
And, indeed, there was/ hardly picture in Rome I was unable/ to reattribute to its rightful owner.
options: to reattribute to its rightful owner.
hardly picture in Rome I was unable
questions.solution: D) The error is the misuse of "hardly". The word "hardly" is an adverb, typically used to mean "only just; almost not". In this context, it seems like the sentence is trying to say that there was almost no picture in Rome that the speaker was unable to reattribute to its rightful owner.

Q13. Select the option that will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement’.
He spent many an hours playing the chess across the city.
options: He have spent many an hours playing the chess across the
He had spent many an hours playing the chess across the
He spent many an hour playing the chess across the
questions.solution:
D) "He spent many an hour playing the chess across the"
The phrase "many an hour" is the correct usage instead of "many an hours". This phrase is used to emphasize the large amount of time spent on something.

Q15. Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.
Such was the education / of the Spartans with regard to / one of the greatest of there kings.
options: one of the greatest of there kings.
of the Spartans with regard to
questions.solution: B) The error is in the sentence part "one of the greatest of there kings." The correct usage should be "their" instead of "there." "Their" is a possessive pronoun used to show ownership, whereas "there" typically refers to a place or position

questions.q:
Q17. Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.
His shoes were soaked from walk through the dew.
questions.solution: A) The phrase "from walk" is incorrect in this context. "Walking" is the correct gerund form to use after "from". Therefore, the correct and improved sentence should be "His shoes were soaked from walking through the dew."

questions.q:
Q19.  Some parts of a few sentences have been jumbled up, and labelled A, B, C and D. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.

I didn’t speak to the sage again for many years,
A. seer, born on a dark island of a union between an ascetic and a fisher princess
B. because of the many hefty books, he’d written. Vyasa the
C. though I heard of him from time to time. I learned
D. his name: Vyasa the Compendious,
questions.solution:
C)CDBA
I didn’t speak to the sage again for many years, though I heard of him from time to time. I learned his name: Vyasa the Compendious, because of the many hefty books, he’d written. Vyasa the seer, born on a dark island of a union between an ascetic and a fisher princess.

questions.q:
Comprehension:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.
I would uncover the story that lay (1) ______ between the lines of the men’s exploits. Better still, I (2) ______ one of them tell it herself, with all her joys and doubts, her struggles and her triumphs, her heartbreaks, her achievements, the unique female way (3) ______ which she sees her world and her place in it. And who could be (4) ______ for this than Panchaali? It is her life, her voice, her questions, and her vision that I invite you (5) ______ 'The Palace of Illusions'.
Q21. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
questions.solution:
D)Invisible
The author wants to uncover (or reveal) the story that isn't immediately apparent or visible to the readers, which lies 'invisible' between the lines of the men's exploits. Therefore, the term 'invisible' conveys this hidden or unseen quality best among the options given.

And who could be (4) ______ for this than Panchaali? It is her life, her voice, her questions, and her vision that I invite you (5) ______ 'The Palace of Illusions'.
Q22. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2
questions.solution:
A)Would have
The passage is discussing the author's desire to uncover the story and have one of the men tell it, but it suggests that an even better option would be to have a woman, specifically Panchaali, tell the story. The phrase "I would have one of them tell it herself" implies that the author would prefer to have a woman tell the story. Therefore, the correct option is "would have."

The phrase "the unique female way in which she sees her world and her place in it" suggests that the author wants to emphasize the perspective or viewpoint of Panchaali as a woman.
